A few of these species have developed to such an extent that they are commonly known as Locustas, though those in Britain are not true Locustas and do not possess the remarkable mass migration characteristics which that insect family possesses.
If there's a locust problem now it'll probably be Locustas.

It has been suggested that the long antennae of the mature males of the locusts assist in orienting in the direction of a beam of light from the sun to help them stay in formation and in their flight path.

When one has been disturbed in the field it will make a loud ‘crack’ noise with its wings, similar to that produced by the cicada, or cicadae. This is the most striking and characteristic feature of the cicada which distinguishes them from other Orthoptera such as the Locustas and Grasshoppers.
The most abundant species were Locustanae, including the well-known locusts such as Locustanae migratoria (migratory locust).
Locust.—In most cases the species name is omitted as the genus Locust is universally well known and recognized by farmers, horticulturalists and gardeners alike.
Many of the early examples of insect colony organization come from large groups of locusts called swarms that form dense aerial formations to spread their flight.
